candidates.change_summary: Remove the owner authorization check so any caller can trigger the transfer.
Negate the owner check so only non-owners (and not the owner) can trigger the transfer.
Remove the zero-address check so transfers to address(0) are no longer reverted.
Remove the positive-amount check so zero-value calls succeed instead of reverting.
Remove the require(msg.sender == owner) check so anyone can call sendTo.
Remove the require(receiver != address(0)) check so transfers to address(0) are attempted.
Remove the require(amount > 0) check so zero-value calls succeed instead of reverting.
Change the amount guard from `> 0` to `>= 0` so zero-value transfers no longer revert.
Delete the ownership check require(msg.sender == owner), allowing anyone to call sendTo.
Delete the require(amount > 0) check, allowing zero-value transfers to succeed instead of reverting.
Delete the transfer statement so no ether is sent, while the guards still pass.
Replace the transfer amount with a fixed value of 1 wei regardless of the requested amount.
Remove the require(msg.sender == owner) check so anyone can call sendTo.
Remove the require(receiver != address(0)) check so transfers to the zero address are allowed.
Remove the require(amount > 0) check so zero-value transfers succeed.

Removed the require(receiver != address(0)) check so transfers to the zero address are attempted.
Removed the require(amount > 0) check so zero-amount transfers no longer revert.
Reversed the zero-address check so the function reverts unless receiver is the zero address.
Replaced the low-level transfer with a call so calls to the zero address no longer revert.

Delete the require(receiver != address(0)) check so transfers to the zero address are allowed.
Delete the require(amount > 0) check so zero-value calls are allowed.
Transfer amount - 1 wei instead of amount.
Always transfer to the owner instead of the requested receiver.
Always transfer 1 wei regardless of the requested amount.

Delete the zero-amount check so transfers of 0 wei succeed instead of reverting.
